That being said, the joy that it brought my niece was well worth it. The price makes me go with four stars. If I was going simply off my niece's enthusiasm, it would easily earn 5 stars.

PLEASE NOTE: To purchase this castle, the family set ($22.99) and the animals (prices vary) will put you well over $60. Something to consider when making the purchase.

text_fidelity_a:
Boom Boom Balloon, Exciting Anticipation Family Board Game Outdoor Summer Toy, for Kids Ages 8 and up My oldest son(5) recently started daily injections. As you would expect, he hates them. We try to do something fun after each of them, and this was used as one of his "surprises". It did the trick and took his mind off that mean needle.

This game is really fun! Not only did my children enjoy it, but I did, too. It does come with a few issues, though.

First of all, as I put the thing together, the instructions say to never use your mouth to blow up the balloon. You must use a balloon pump. A balloon pump isn't included, so I chose to use my mouth to blow up the balloon, since I had excited children waiting to play. It went fine. I was able to blow up the balloon while it was in the frame without any problem.

Secondly, we couldn't get the top clip piece to stay put. There's a clip that holds the 3 pieces of the frame together at the top. It kept coming lose no matter how tight I tried to get it. When I took the thing apart, I couldn't get one frame piece to come apart. So, 2 were so lose the whole thing kept coming apart, but one was so tight I had to put it in the box together, and therefore, couldn't close the lid.

Third, one of the sticks was broke within minutes of playing the game. Thankfully, there are 4 extras included, so we can still play. Plus, the recommended age is 8 and up. I played this game with my 2 and 5 year olds. The 2 year old is the one that broke the stick, so I'm not taking stars off for that issue or anything. It's simply to warn you that they do break pretty easily.

There are 12 balloons included. They are all the same: blue, with a face. They are the regular sized balloons, so I imagine this game will work perfectly fine with store bought replacement balloons. You just probably won't have a face on there.

I know it sounds like a lot of complaining up there, but we really enjoyed this game!

The basics: You put the thing together, which is really simple. You put the balloon in the frame, blow it up, and then wrap it around the "hook" at the bottom to keep the air in without having to actually tie it. Super simple. You take the sticks and put them in the holes(6) until you hear the first click. Then you take turns rolling dice. Whatever number it lands on is the amount of times you push in a stick. It can be the same stick or one click each on different sticks. Whoever pops the balloon first loses(or wins if you're my children).

Overall, it's a fun game that's worth the issues that come with it.
text_fidelity_b: Boom Boom Balloon, Exciting Anticipation Family Board Game Outdoor Summer Toy, for Kids Ages 8 and up

text_fidelity_a:
Friendly Loom Lotta Loops 7" Traditional Size Bright Cotton Loops Makes 8 Potholders, Weaving, Crafts for Kids and Adults by Harrisville Designs We've been making potholders at home and it seemed like we were always running out of the colors we wanted, so we ordered replacements from several different sources to see what worked best. Although these are not the easiest to use, they by far make the best finished product. This is a great big bag of loops with very vibrant colors. The colors are great -- teal, cobalt, lime green, kelly green, pink, red, reddish-purple, yellow, orange -- enough to make some beautiful combinations. Compared to the other loops we've used, these are very thick and less stretchy. Because they are bulkier, they are a little harder to work with. I haven't found any that don't fit, though. On the flip side, the finished potholder is larger and holds its shape better. I've found that the stretchier brands seem to have a lot of nylon, and it doesn't seem like they'd hold up as well to hot dishes. These loops are kind of scraggly, with loose threads hanging off of them, but when you weave them together the loose threads aren't really a problem.

Someone commented that her daughter wasn't able to weave the edges with these because they were less stretchy. My daughter hasn't been able to weave the edges with these either, but she's very, very proud of the finished product as it is larger, more vibrant, and more even in shape than the potholders made with the stretchier loops.

If you want something that's really easy to use, you might check for the loops made by klutz or others, as these might not be the best bet. If you want to make cool potholders, though, these are a good choice.

UPDATE: I'm back a year later to buy more. Glad that I was able to find the good loops again. And now that my daughter is 8, she no longer has difficulty weaving the edges -- most of the time. Also, these are much easier to weave off the edges when you use the metal loom, rather than the plastic ones.

UPDATE #2: Almost two years later, and my daughter is back making potholders, this time trying to create her own designs. Need more loops!
text_fidelity_b: Friendly Loom Lotta Loops 7" Traditional Size Bright Cotton Loops Makes 8 Potholders, Weaving, Crafts for Kids and Adults by Harrisville Designs

As a die hard Star Wars Fan this Saber has a lot going for it, but a few cons. First the build and look are nice. The sound is also very good. The price is one of the best reasons for getting one. As of today a 40% off coupon making it around $72.00. To me at this price point shows you how much Disney and Star Wars The Black Series is ripping people off.

For the $72.00 you're getting 12 Light Sabers "colors" compare that to $250.00 and higher for one color. Now for the cons the blade is held in place by three set screws and it still has a bit of a lose feeling not much but its there. The other thing is the control button it is a bit cumbersome and by that I mean the holding down or pushing or doing the fast twist while holding button down to change sound fonts. I know some other saber makers use similar features but not this hard to change. One of the sound fonts is not even from Star Wars. I did not know what it was and could not stand it, but you might like. The problem was it took me several tries to change it and it should not be that hard to change.

So even with those two minor faults, this is still a great Saber for the price. As someone who was 10 years old when Star Wars came out, even now holding this and turning it on makes me smile.

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Kanoodle Jr. Brain Boosting Puzzle Game, Brain Teaser Game for Kids Teens, & Adults, 2-D & 3-D Puzzles, Great For Travel, Gift For Kids Ages 4 to 7 What a great puzzle. Kanoodle is a one-player game in which you take 6 tetris-like pieces and use them to fill in a pattern on the square board. There are 60 puzzles in this group, all included in a book form. I do have a few minor issues, enough to remove one star:

- The puzzles are delivered in the form of a book. There are multiple languages of instructions inside, then you get to the puzzles. Each puzzle is well-done, but the book itself is not the ideal way of presenting the puzzles. Since you're either balancing the book on the shelf above the board, or pulling it out or putting it back underneath the board, it gets scuffed, torn and bent up rather quickly. On day 3, our book looks like a mess. It should have been thicker cards with a separate rulebook.

- Some kids will master this quickly. My four-year-old is on 4-star puzzles already, and we've owned the game for less than 3 days. I think she'll be stuck here for a decent while, and she does enjoy going back to re-do easier puzzles, but I think she's got the hang of it quickly. Yesterday, she completed puzzle 43 out of 60, and they're ordered by difficulty.

This review may sound negative, but let me emphasize that THIS IS SUCH A GOOD TOY! You can see the wheels turning in my daughter's brain as she tries to figure out how to make it work. If you're going on a road trip, this is a must.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Kanoodle Jr. Brain Boosting Puzzle Game, Brain Teaser Game for Kids Teens, & Adults, 2-D & 3-D Puzzles, Great For Travel, Gift For Kids Ages 4 to 7

He loves his cars and so this was a nice compact "repair garage" play structure. It will not be something you will want to break down daily and store, it will need to be up and available for immediate play. It will stay at my house for his visits and be stored on a closet shelf between visits. It came with one little tow truck vehicle. There is no car storage; this is just a play activity. A turning knob on top of the elevator brings cars up to individual floor levels and there are gates on the ramps that divert the cars to a car maintenance floor and a car wash floor in the structure. Although it says it's 4 level, there is nothing but a ramp from the elevator on the upper level and the lower level is really just the entry to the elevator and an open accessible area underneath that the imagination can invent a use for.

The instructions were also less than stellar and being only in black and white, identifying some of the little pieces was sometimes guesswork. There are small pieces that can be pulled off, so observe the recommended age group for this toy. We were not interested in all the many decorative stickers that can be applied on this toy, so only used what we wanted to.

It appears to be sturdy enough and, if incorporated with some other play structures, could keep his attention for a lengthy period of play time.

- The size - It fits perfectly on top of their school books and doesn't take up a ton of extra space.

text_fidelity_a:
PlayMonster Break in™ Alcatraz Make sure you know what you are getting yourself into before purchasing this item. I think it is a great item for the right person/people. If you are the type of person who likes participating in an escape room, or think you might like to participate in an escape room, then this might be for you. But this is not a game of chance. There is no luck. You do not roll the dice, or pick a card. You must complete each task before continuing. You either get the task right, or wrong. If you get it wrong, then there are hints to help, if you choose to use them.

It takes about 2 hours to complete. It could take you more time if you don’t use the hints, and perhaps less time if you do use the hints. It’s played with between one and 6 players. Honestly, I think 6 players would be too many. If you had 6, I think four would be playing the game and two would be making sure the drinks and snacks keep flowing. ;-)

Once you complete this game, you will not play it again, because you already know how to complete all of the tasks. But you certainly could give it to friends who have not played it. Or, perhaps you could invite other friends over who had not played it before and you could assist them with it.

Once you remove the lid, you will find the different pieces. But do NOT open the box that is inside until you are given instructions to do so. There are tasks which must be completed before you open the box that is inside.

If you want to have an idea of how to get started, then I highly recommend that you do an online search for “Unfiltered Gamer Break In Alcatraz”. These are a couple of guys who will walk you through about the first 20 minutes. If you don’t want to go that far then you can simply watch until they have completed the 1st task so you know exactly what you need to do. Yes, this can be a little complicated, but if you at least watch them complete the 1st task, you’ll know how to get started.
text_fidelity_b: PlayMonster Break in™ Alcatraz

Hot Wheels Race Crate with 3 Stunts in 1 Set Portable Storage Ages 6 to 10 Adult review: it's fast. So fast it's over before it starts. I was most interested in the 4 lane gravity drop and it works perfectly. People complaining cars won't loop may not be trying different cars. After picking different cars a few times I have several that loop correctly. The two that came with it also loop correctly. Some of the longer cars don't seem to make it.

This is one of the neatest designs I've ever seen from Hot Wheels. If you wanted the 6 lane kit that's over 200 dollars from scalpers now...this is a pretty great one to settle for. My only complaints on the gravity drop are it's so fast it's really hard to watch and if you're at the starting end...the large solid loop prevents you from seeing the cars until the hit the finish line. If the loop were clear that would be awesome. I also added some old '68 track and will add more....the cars clear the finish with lots of go power left. Add more track :)

I ended up liking the drag race configuration best with added track.

I believe it is sturdy and it's a pretty big track in any configuration. The fact it all folds into itself for storage is the truly awesome part. Room for several cars in there as well.

Good product for young and old Hot Wheels fans and I wish it had been cheaper but feel I got my money's worth. If kids don't lose any of the few loose pieces....I would imagine it will hold value.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Race Crate with 3 Stunts in 1 Set Portable Storage Ages 6 to 10

text_fidelity_a: Brainwaves: The Astute Goose - A Kosmos Game from Thames & Kosmos | Fun, Scientist Approved, Family-Friendly Games to Sharpen Your Mind & Train Your Brain, for Ages 8+ This card game can be played solo or with up to five players. It is intended for ages eight and up. The large cards are easy to hold and the things you're supposed to memorize on each card are clear to see. There are 25 suspect cards which include variations in color, clothing, and animals. You place three to six of these cards out (depending on the difficulty level you desire) and memorize each card before turning them upside down. There are six number cards that you place above each suspect so that you know which suspect to talk about when you roll the dice. The dice roll tells you which suspect to talk about and which feature (color, clothing, or animal) that you need to remember correctly for that suspect. If the player is able to correctly remember that feature, they keep the card and score a point, but if they remember wrong, the rest of the players each have a chance to guess until someone gets it right or no one does. That suspect card is replaced with a new one, and everyone has a chance to look at the new card. Thus, you are constantly having to remember new information for each position. This can be a fun way to train your brain to remember better, but some people might find it too frustrating.
text_fidelity_b: Brainwaves: The Astute Goose - A Kosmos Game from Thames & Kosmos | Fun, Scientist Approved, Family-Friendly Games to Sharpen Your Mind & Train Your Brain, for Ages 8+

text_fidelity_a:
Westcott 6" Titanium Precision Scissors - Violet I’m a crafter and a super office supply freak. I confess this so you will understand that I have a LOT of scissors. It is a well known fact that you need different scissors for different types of project. It’s also fact that there is something slightly wrong with every pair. It’s one of those mysteries like when you put a pair of socks in the dryer only one comes out. Head scratcher.
Against all odds, and the rules of the crafting universe, these scissors are perfect.
The handle is big enough for any size fingers. The grip is so comfortable I have not had a case of the “scissor cramps” no matter how long I use them for.
The blades are super sharp, aaaaallll the way down to the tips. They allow me to snip into the most minute 'V' of a paper cut out. Even better they let me cut the most clean appliqués for quilting. No need to tear out that last little bit of paper you couldn’t get with your scissors. I’m so used to doing that it now feels like I’m missing a step. They cut cleanly through even my thickest macrame cord, which is why I bought them in the first place.
The anti-stick is no joke. These are now my exclusive washi tape cutting scissors. I don’t need to get out the rubbing alcohol or Goof-Off to wipe down the blades to get the adhesive off. It simply doesn’t stick to the blades at all. It’s a miracle!
When I was first looking at these to buy them I giggled a bit about the lanyard, like who would use that? The answer is me! I use the lanyard! Most of the time I have them hanging right next to my workspace where I can grab them easy peasy. But I find myself putting it around my neck when I’m moving around. It keeps the sharp point safe and they don’t get lost under the inevitable mess I make. And when I’m working on a large macrame project I don’t need to drop the cord to get the scissors.
Now don’t shake your head, I haven’t lost my mind entirely, I don’t use them for tape/paper AND fabric. That would be up there with drinking orange juice then brushing my teeth. No, instead I simply bought two pairs. The orange/grey for fabric and the purple/pink for everything else. I probably could’ve used the same pair but why upset the balance of the universe, amma right?
Will these replace all of your scissors? Nope. But they for sure will replace all your smaller pairs. I definitely recommend getting these, in all available colors!
text_fidelity_b: Westcott 6" Titanium Precision Scissors - Violet

text_fidelity_a:
Mafia de Cuba This is a pretty good bluffing and betrayal game, along the lines of the Resistance, Werewolf, or for those who are less familiar with board games, maybe even Liar's Dice or the similarly themed Cash and Guns. You get a nice looking cigar box, a bunch of poker chips and a surprisingly light little rule book that packs a lot of fiddly into a very small package (You can do this, or if you do that, you can do between one and three types of thingy, unless you've already taken the what'sit and then refer to page three).

Overall, a very fun and short game if:
1. You have a well-chosen and probably an experienced player be the don. There is actually quite a lot to this role, and a lot of consultation with that fiddly little rule about what you can initially take. The rest of the game is super simple, but first time players will want to see a round first. The person playing as the don has to basically command the entire game, so choosing a shy or confused player can completely ruin the experience.
2. You like the Resistance and games similar, but want something just a little different. This will provide that.
3. You have a group large enough to play this 6 - 12 player game. It handles double digits quite well.
text_fidelity_b: Mafia de Cuba

1st - I don’t know why companies create toys for kids 3+ that include markers that aren’t washable!!

2nd - the main (black) dry erase maker is the only one that is a complete handled marker with an eraser lid. The other 4 markers have a 1.5” handle area to hold onto. The markers work and erase well.
The markers are hard to get back into their elastic straps. It’s difficult to do as an adult- let alone a 3+yo. An additional 1/4” of elastic would have been helpful.

3rd - the activity pages have a spiral binding. The way it is set up the last page is attached to the back of the kit - I like this. But the spiral is too small to allow the pages to tuck behind the kit and the top of the pages lift up from the back of the bottom.
The pages are sometimes used together for a project but not always.

4th - there isn’t a bag or something to store the magnets that aren’t being used.
The magnets are all on 2 sheets and are very strong. You can easily layer these magnets to get different looks. There are 54 magnets so it would be nice if there was an area built in to store the magnets while they aren’t being used.

5th - This activity pad takes a lot of space and is larger than a child’s lap - it’s 23” wide. It would be nice if the pad could be opened and folded in half.

6th - the velcro closure is nice and strong but the cardboard tab is weaker than it needs to be. I worry that after much use this tab will be ripped off.

All that being said - this activity pad is nice.
It’s a good quiet time activity that has a lot of fun included.
My daughter takes this to restaurants and plane rides to keep her busy!
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Natural Play: Play, Draw, Create Reusable Drawing & Magnet Kit – Ocean (42 Magnets, 5 Dry-Erase Markers)

Three AAA batteries are needed to power the drill according to the instruction manual, and two AAA batteries are needed for the train engine for the sound and light. The wheels roll smoothly and securely, and it is easy to connect the three sections of the train together, so it is a good toy not just a building activity. There are some extra bolts in case some are lost. The train is sturdy and can withstand the rough treatment of a 3-year-old armed with a plastic hammer.

Fisher-Price Loving Family Dollhouse As a new dad with no sisters growing up, I'm fairly new to the whole dollhouse experience. While I would have loved (although not necessarily expected) some karate-chop action in the parent figures, or flamethrower accessories, this is a pretty cool looking fortress, no wait, I mean dollhouse, and my daughter loves it, even if she doesn't understand why GI Joe keeps trying to rappel up to the 4th floor balcony with his grappling hook. .

Seriously though, she really does love this dollhouse. There are some family members included, but only parents and baby, who appears to have just come from the hospital. It's a bit like a family just moving into their first apartment, where all they have is a moldy old sofa and some flowers on the wall.

Everything that she wants to play with is, of course, something I have to buy separately. That's a bit annoying, but typical I suppose, although someone with more experience in these sorts of girl-fortresses might know of a better alternative. Practically speaking, Cobra Commander and Skelator could just waltz right in the front door, as there are no missile launchers, so those must come in one of the accessory packs.

text_fidelity_a:
Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome This is a fun ride-on toy for kids. I like that it sits close to the ground, which makes it better for younger kids, but the design is still “cool” enough that older kids will still like it. The dune buggy has a lot of good features. First, the blue color will appeal to both girls and boys. The vehicle has two speeds, which is nice. However, the parent lock-out needs to be removed to access the higher speed. The lock-out is a screw that’s fairly difficult to remove because of its location. The higher speed is definitely needed to easily ride in the wet grass, even on flat ground. It’s fairly easy to steer the vehicle and is a lot of fun for kids to drive.

To stop the vehicle, take your foot off the gas pedal. It will still slide a little on pavement, possibly because of the plastic wheels. It also will continue to slowly roll going downhill, even on a small incline. That’s why even though the guidelines say ages 3 to 7, I would use caution for younger kids unless you have a large, flat area with no nearby hills. Older kids, up to 11 or 12, will like it, too. However, with the position of the steering wheel, their height will determine how well they’ll comfortably fit in the dune buggy and be able to easily steer.

Be sure to charge the battery the night before using the first time. The battery only lasted about 15 minutes right out of the box after being putting the car together. I also learned the hard way that the dune buggy is heavy to push if it does bog down or if the battery dies. (The battery is rechargeable battery, but there isn’t a battery indicator, so I wasn’t expecting it to go dead so quickly.)

Once the dune buggy is assembled and the battery is charged, it’s a lot of fun for kids. The assembly is a chore for adults, though. I took almost an hour and a half to assemble. Most of that time was spent putting on the wheels. The directions aren’t clear and some of the screws are hard to get to and there isn’t room to use an electric screwdriver. As long as you allow enough time for assembly and charging the battery, this dune buggy will be a hit.
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome

LeapFrog LeapStart Interactive Learning System, Pink My grandmother purchased these as a special gift for 2 girls ages just turned 2 and almost 4 as there was some resentment from their new baby brother. She told me there were many good reviews and thought it could help the girls stay busy when Mommy needs to help their brother. These are a life saver. We even got the headphones to match so there is not fights over I can't hear my book because of your book. It was also amazing we got 2 system to solve fights. I just took a label maker and put each of their names on them.

They did get the first series of books. However the almost 4 year old is flying through the books as they are easy for her. So we just got one next level up book and that seems to be more her speed. Each system we were able to download 10 books and the sample book. Unfortunately it won't fit more. So as the older one gets more advanced, we will delete the younger books.

The system does take AA batteries, so I suggest keeping a spare set on hand. The downside is there is no warning of low battery, so it helps to have new ones ready to go. You also need a small screw driver to put them in.

I also suggest getting (or making as I did) a tote bag for them to store their system and books in.

The device is easy to open. They do need assistance with the books sometimes. I do wish the stylus pen cord was a bit longer, but that may be a safety thing too so the kids don't get hurt.

text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Empire Game [[VIDEOID:8f653ee987e2df8b52e209e097da8a22]] This is such a cool game! It's a scaled down version of Monopoly, and each game only takes 5-15 minutes to play, instead of the hours of a regular Monopoly game. So you'll hear something with this Monopoly game that you won't hear with any other Monopoly game, which is "Want to play again?"

It still captures the essence of Monopoly, so it still feels like a Monopoly game. It's more of a social game than a strategy game, but that will make it more fun for more people.

They've taken out the property cards, and replaced them with little tiles and a tower. The number of tiles, not the original value of the tile, determine how much that you pay when you land on someone else's property. The old Community Chest cards are now Empire cards, and you get a couple to hold on to at the start of the game, and you can use these strategically, and do various combos with them.

It's very fun, and I liked it a lot. If you get just one game this year, this should be the game you pick.

Pros:
+Excellent instructions
+Extremely well designed
+Has cool brands like Fender, Nerf, and Coke
+Quick version of Monopoly (I never thought I'd ever use quick and Monopoly in the same sentence.)
+They did an awesome job of play testing this game. It's very balanced and very fun. Whoever worked on the team that made this game should be promoted.

Cons:
-Less strategy than regular Monopoly, but it is more fun for more people
-Because it's subsidized by advertising, they really should be giving this game away. But, the advertising isn't as annoying as in other games.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Empire Game

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Shelby’s Snack Shack Game and Board Book Combo: Preschool Math Game, Board Game & Board Book, Ages 4+ We'd already bought the Sneaky Squirrel Game, which is similar to this game. We've though it was one of the cutest games ever, so we were thrilled to add this one to our collection, too!

With this game, you'll get one of the cutest boxes you've ever seen! (Let me note here that the top and bottom of the game box do NOT fit inside each other. It's the same with the squirrel game.) You'll also get a super cute pair of Shelby tweezers, 4 bowls, a packet of bones, and a double spinner.

Playing the game is pretty simple. There can be up to 4 players at a time. Each player will spin first to see if they will get bones or lose bones or just lose a turn. The second spin is to determine how many bones they will win/lose. If they land on a seagull, it means they will lose bones. If they land on the hungry pug, they get to steal bones from another player. Busy pug means they lose a turn, and landing on the bones mean they win bones for their bowl. They can pick up the bones they win/lose with the tweezers.

The tweezers are a great way to develop motor skills. The game itself is a great, fun way to learn counting skills. My 5 year old is delayed and really struggles with numbers, so I'm always thrilled to find a new, exciting way to teach them to him. This is also a fun game for my 2 year old. It IS pretty simple, so I imagine, on average, 2-4, maybe 5, is probably the best ages for this game.

Overall, this is a super cute game! I can highly recommend this AND the Sneaky Squirrel Game for your young little ones!
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Shelby’s Snack Shack Game and Board Book Combo: Preschool Math Game, Board Game & Board Book, Ages 4+

It was easy to assemble, thanks to the wonderful instructions, and we had it ready to go in maybe fifteen minutes. Everything worked right out of the box. It has a working fm radio and an audio jack to plug in a phone or MP3 player. The lights are functional and controlled by a switch. The steering wheel has a horn button and two sound effect buttons. The gear shift has options for reverse and first and second gears. There’s a safety on it that keeps your child from going into fast mode on accident. You have to remove the little piece with a screwdriver for it to work. I appreciate when companies go that extra mile to make things safer. I’ve always been a fan of Radio Flyer products but until about two months ago, I didn’t even know Radio Flyer made this type of product. Now that I do, I’m thrilled to have such a nice, safe car for my little man. He’s been having so much fun with it and it definitely deserves my highest recommendation.
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer Riptide Car | Outdoor Power Ride On Toy | Ages 3+ (Amazon Exclusive) Red

Barbie Dream Closet Playset with 30+ Clothes and Accessories Including 5 Outfits, Plus Mirror, Desk and Rotating Rack The Barbie Dream Closet is indeed a very happy dream realized. There’s so much space to store all of the clothes and accessories, as well any additional clothing items you already own for Barbie. The mini hangers work great with the clothing rack, as there’s a bit of a grip to the hooks so the hangers stay in place, but are easy to put on and take off. The system is also super convenient to carry around due to its folded design, which latches in the front with a Barbie labeled lever, and the handle on top lets this go anywhere with ease. I do love that this set encourages all sorts of ways to be fun, adventurous, sporty, fancy, and smart with the closet decals, clothes and accessories (lab coat and shoes, laptop, fancy dress with jewelry and shoes, scuba gear, etc).

A few criticisms though…the nob on top to turn the clothing rack is a bit hard to spin, both in resistance and due to the short nob. I do wish it was a little bit looser and the nob was a little bit taller to make it easier to grab.
There are a few areas that fold in and out for storage, as well as shelves to place things, but I think it would have been nice for some sort of drawer system. The drawers would have been helpful for storing the mini bracelet, necklace, hair brush, sunglasses, etc to give them a good home when not in use. Using my imagination, it would have been extra fun if the full-length mirror had a battery operated set of mini Hollywood lights to add some flare. I think some extra touches like the drawers and mirror lights would make the price worth it. I think it’s just a tad on the expensive side for it lacking some details, although it's worth reiterating that the included pieces offer a lot of good play and imagination.

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Labyrinth Family Board Game for Kids and Adults Age 7 and Up - Millions Sold, Easy to Learn and Play with Great Replay Value (26448) So....I'm Gen X and we played the original version some in college along with games like Risk and Stratego on weekends. It isnt quite a fluff game but it isnt very hard. I would think both children and adults would enjoy this game. A game adults can enjoy with their kids....or a fun starter game or game for chatting and having a beverage or three.

The best part is there is hardly any explanation needed to get started. Move tiles to open a path to get to the objects on your cards. And....block others from their goals. I love this game especially with 3 or 4 people instead of two. It requires some strategy but luck can make or break it, too.

Harry Potter version! Yes! Well...it is beautiful. The board looks wonderful! But in this version you are gathering "people" or characters rather than treasure items. The premise makes sense. Going through the maze that is Hogwarts gathering people ....you must match cards in your hands to pics on the tiles of the gameboard. Sounds AWESOME. In reality...it is kind of messy because some people look similar. Some people are the big characters...such as Harry or Snape....there were 3 I was like....who on earth is THIS and I thought I was a big fan. So....due to the pics on the game board being rather small....they are also color coded too. If your card is Harry with a blue border....Harry has a blue border on the game tile as well. But is there another character who looks very similar on the board with a blue border? Yes there is. So....yeah, it is really cool BUT pay good attention as the character pictures certainly are NOT as easy to discern as a scarab or diamond in the original. Hey...but it looks great!

I give this game 10 out of 10 because my gripes do not effect the game. If you are are a HP fan....and you already like or think you might like a labyrinth game...here ya go. This is 100% Ravensburg quality. The box is good quality as all the pieces. The box holds everything in the usual labyrinth organized way. Very nice.

At the price point....I really, really, really dont like wooden pegs. They are sort of big, bright and easy to move but I liked the Labyrinth version with the plastic characters NOT the one with wooden pegs. I have no idea WHY if your player piece coincides with a house....such as Slytherin....they didnt atleast make little plastic coats of armor for each house. I just hate generic pegs in fun games. But it doesnt make the game any better or worse. I saw some reviews where people complained about the card quality. It is the same it always has been. The cards are simply there to identify your next goal. This game doesnt require shuffling like Uno or slapping...or grabbing or swapping cards. They are perfectly fine.

Great game. Great Ravensburger quality. Dear Ravensburger.....I sure would love a Scooby Doo version with cool plastic player pieces!

I included pics and pics of game pieces from an earlier version of the original game
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Labyrinth Family Board Game for Kids and Adults Age 7 and Up - Millions Sold, Easy to Learn and Play with Great Replay Value (26448)
